question.problem:
The following table shows the speed $v$, in $\text{km/min},$ at certain times during a family car trip over a period of $60$ minutes.

| $t\,(\text{min})$ | $60$ | $70$ | $80$ | $95$ | $110$ | $120$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v\,(\text{km/min})$ | $1.5$ | $2$ | $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $1.5$ |

Assuming that the family traveled $130\,\text{km}$ during the first hour of the trip, use the left Riemann sum to approximate the total distance traveled during the first two hours.

*Hint: The distance traveled is given by the area under the speed-time graph.*

current_example.problem:
The following table shows some values of a continuous function $f(x)$ over the interval $[0,2].$

| $x$ | $0$ | $0.8$ | $1.6$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $2$ | $5$ | $10$ | $12$ |

Use the left Riemann sum, with the three subintervals indicated by the data, to approximate the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ over the interval $[0,2].$
current_example.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=3$ rectangles. Using the left Riemann sum, the area is computed as

$$
\mathcal{A}	\approx	f(0.0)\Delta x_1+f(0.8)\Delta x_2+f(1.6)\Delta x_3,
$$

where each $\Delta x_i$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $x$-value and the next one, i.e.,

$$
\Delta x_i = x_{i+1}-x_{i}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $\Delta x$'s.

| $x$ | $0$ | $0.8$ | $1.6$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\Delta{x}$ | $0.8$ | $0.8$ | $0.4$ | $-$ |
| $f(x)$ | $2$ | $5$ | $10$ | $12$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈2\cdot 0.8+5\cdot 0.8+10\cdot 0.4 \\  & =1.6+4+4 \\  & =9.6.\end{aligned}
$$
